correctness.rationale: From Wang's exact diamond conflict criterion, two disjoint edges must differ in color exactly when at least three connector edges are present. For complete multipartite graphs, disjoint edges lying in different unordered part-pairs have at least three connectors, whereas distinct disjoint edges in one fixed bipartite cut have precisely two. Therefore the entire edge-conflict graph is the graph join of L(K_{n_i,n_j}) across unordered part pairs. Chromatic numbers add over a join; bipartite cut K_{a,b} has ordinary chromatic index max(a,b), shown by a proper cyclic modulo max(a,b) coloring and the max-degree lower bound. Sorting parts gives sum_{i<j}max(n_i,n_j)=sum_{i<r}(r-i)n_i. With s=r-1 and Delta=sum_{i=1}^s n_i, the difference from Delta(Delta+1)/2 is >=(Delta-s)(Delta-s+1)/2; equality forces all parts singleton. Inspected verifier reconstructs adjacency via all four connectors, uses exact coloring on isomorphism types up to 7 vertices (37 types) and explicit valid colorings through 10 (128 types); these are finite checks only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Wang proves a universal coarser quadratic upper bound and conjectures a sharper universal one; Tian–Wang improves a sufficiently-large-degree bound. A general bound does not imply this exact multipartite value and structure. The triangle-free bipartite endpoint is already classical.
